title: std::optional
recap: std::optional<T> represents either a T value or no value. It avoids sentinel ambiguity, especially when every ordinary T value could be a valid result.
Check engagement before dereferencing or use value_or when a fallback is appropriate. An engaged optional containing zero is still engaged.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement parseDigit(character). For ASCII characters 0..9 return an engaged std::optional<int> containing the numeric digit. For any other character return std::nullopt. An engaged zero is a valid result and is different from an empty optional.
hints: Use character bounds to recognize digits.
Subtract the character zero, not numeric zero.
